clue.text: Cheers beginning in Pennsylvania, America saw British in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole string is read from right to left
the beginning of the word Pennsylvania supplies its first letter

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or maxim, a motto

explanation.surface: Somebody watches British forces retreating at the start of a campaign in Pennsylvania and raises a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns round the whole string PUSMOTTOB. 'saw' is the noun for a proverb, not the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast, said as glasses are raised and emptied, so it serves as an exclamation like cheers.

clue.text: Very much cake, case of forty or fifty eaten up

indicators.note: the bar eats the reversed pair, which goes inside it

parts.note: a cake of soap is a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
the case of a phrase is its outside, the first and last letters of the words forty or fifty

explanation.surface: A cake has been eaten by somebody aged forty or fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the outer letters of the phrase 'forty or fifty', F and Y; 'up' turns them to YF, which goes into BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom intensifying a comparison, as in 'by a long way', meaning greatly or to a large degree.

clue.text: Sailor welcomes artillery and flag waving in battle

indicators.note: a sailor welcoming guests takes them in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: a waving flag moves about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor hails gunners and waves a flag during a naval battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' signals the anagram and 'welcomes' the container. The Royal Artillery is a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar is the 1805 naval engagement off Spain where Nelson defeated the French and Spanish fleets.

clue.text: Our cinema's about to screen a display of marine life

indicators.note: screening something hides it behind or within, so the letter a goes inside
about signals that the letters of our cinema are moved around

explanation.surface: A local cinema is about to show a documentary about sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges OURCINEMA, and 'to screen' puts A inside the result. 'about to' looks like 'soon going to', but the words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A large aquarium for sea creatures, open to the public, is exactly a showcase of ocean life.

clue.text: Priest about right as adventurer

indicators.note: the priest goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: a shaman is a priest or healer in some traditional religions

explanation.surface: A priest who is fairly upright is cast as a daring explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen Sharman was the first British astronaut, in 1991; the puzzle's adventurers are all space travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts space travellers as adventurers; this British astronaut flew to the Mir station.

clue.text: Couple after Macedonian leader in Alexander, say, finding buried treasure in Italy?

indicators.note: the pair is placed after the rest
the Macedonian letter goes inside the word for a pontiff

parts.note: Alexander was the name of several popes, so the word stands for a pope

indicators.note: the leader of the word Macedonian is its first letter

parts.note: a couple is two, Roman numeral II

explanation.surface: A couple go after Alexander the Great and find hidden riches in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alexander' and 'Macedonian' suggest Alexander the Great, but Alexander is a papal name: M goes into POPE. The city buried by Vesuvius is a treasure trove for archaeologists, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman city entombed in ash in AD 79 is a priceless archaeological site, a figurative buried treasure.

clue.text: Land between mountains with northern adventurer

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, chiefly in Scotland

explanation.surface: An explorer from the north crosses a valley in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: John Glenn was the first American to orbit the Earth, in 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme treats astronauts as adventurers; this one was a pioneer of NASA's Mercury programme.

clue.text: Sound way to walk in door

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for a manner of walking is heard, not seen

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking

explanation.surface: Advice on the right way to walk through a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged barrier closing an opening in a wall or fence works as an outdoor door.

clue.text: Biblical character, one turning on the house of God

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
turning the word one back to front

parts.note: a church is the house of God, abbreviated CH

explanation.surface: A single figure from the Bible turns against the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the word one, and in a down clue 'on' places it above the abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the father of Methuselah, said to have walked with God and been taken up.

clue.text: Bedtime drinks for birds

parts.note: night is when people go to bed
jars is informal British for glasses of beer

explanation.surface: A nightcap or two for the pet birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a jar' is everyday British slang for a drink, usually a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal insect-eating birds with churring calls, also known as goatsuckers, are a family of birds.

clue.text: Potential Mount Everest, primarily for adventurer

parts.note: a foal is a young horse, so a mount in the making

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word Everest

explanation.surface: An explorer eyeing a possible climb of Mount Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount Everest' reads as one name, but 'Potential Mount' is a young horse. Michael Foale is a British-born NASA astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts astronauts as adventurers; this one served on Mir and the International Space Station.

clue.text: Adventurer who packs a punch?

parts.note: a space traveller whose surname, split, suggests powerful limbs that could throw a heavy blow

explanation.surface: An explorer known for hitting hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Armstrong was the first man on the Moon; his surname read as strong arms explains the punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts astronauts as adventurers, and this name read in two parts describes someone with a mighty blow.

clue.text: Spooner's dance with 10, rational figure

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade their initial consonants

parts.note: 10 across is Armstrong, whose first name was Neil
the rumba is a Cuban dance

explanation.surface: A dance with a partner described as a rational figure, as Spooner might say it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of RUMBA and NEIL gives NUMBA and REIL, heard as the answer's two words.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics every rational number is one of the reals, so a rational figure is an example of the class.

clue.text: Note success after first from Cambridge

indicators.note: the word for success comes after the first letter
first from takes the opening letter of the word Cambridge

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A note of congratulation for a student's success at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written memo or voucher, such as an IOU, is a brief note.

clue.text: Spring chicken's top and stockings new, carefully selected

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: the top of the word chicken is its first letter

parts.note: hose is a word for stockings

explanation.surface: A young woman in new stockings picked out with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring chicken' reads as a young person, but 'Spring' is a well and 'chicken's top' its first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or gifts picked with thought and care are apt, a compound adjective for something judiciously picked.

clue.text: In spirit, the stuff feeding culture for an adventurer

indicators.note: the culture medium goes in the spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit
agar is the jelly on which bacterial cultures are grown

explanation.surface: Somebody steeped in gin and high culture is cast as an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'culture' suggests the arts, but it is a lab culture of bacteria. Yuri Gagarin was the first human in space, in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts astronauts as adventurers, and this Soviet cosmonaut made the first ever orbit of the Earth.

clue.text: Eatery, however briefly, left sink upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the whole string is read from the bottom up
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: but means however
port is the left side of a ship
to sag is to sink

explanation.surface: A restaurant, however small, has a sink fitted upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter; the whole string, BUPORTSAG, is then turned by 'upside down'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub that serves good food is a kind of restaurant, so a type of eating place.

clue.text: Fizzy diet drinks cold, each a cold drink

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the letter for cold goes inside
a fizzy drink bubbles, so the letters of diet are stirred up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone sips fizzy diet drinks cold, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fizzy' gives IEDT, and 'drinks' takes in the letter for cold to make ICEDT. 'cold' also appears in the definition, a deliberate reuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled tea served with ice is a refreshing beverage taken cold.

clue.text: Ingesting tail of pterodactyl, three taste a fossilised arthropod

indicators.note: the group of three swallows the letter, which goes inside

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

indicators.note: the tail of the word pterodactyl is its last letter

parts.note: a bite is a taste, a small mouthful

explanation.surface: Three creatures nibble at a pterodactyl's tail before turning to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: These extinct sea creatures with three-lobed bodies are known only from fossils of the Palaeozoic era.

clue.text: Possible source of wind resistance in jets

indicators.note: the resistance letter goes in the word for jets

parts.note: spouts are jets of liquid
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Wind resistance encountered by jet aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks aeronautical, but it means flatulence: Brussels sprouts are notorious for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels vegetables are famous for causing flatulence, so they may well be behind some wind.

clue.text: Normal to jettison sandwiches as adventurer

indicators.note: the word for jettison sandwiches the normal standard between its letters

parts.note: to shed is to jettison or cast off
par is the normal standard

explanation.surface: An explorer who normally throws away sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shepard was the first American in space, in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts astronauts as adventurers; this one later walked on the Moon with Apollo 14.

clue.text: Change round Lithuanian and Latvian capitals, as adventurer

indicators.note: the coins go round the two capital letters

parts.note: change means loose coins

indicators.note: capitals are the first letters of the words Lithuanian and Latvian

explanation.surface: An explorer changes money in the Baltic capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' suggests Vilnius and Riga, but means initial letters, L and L. Eileen Collins was the first woman to command a space shuttle.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts astronauts as adventurers; this NASA pilot flew several space shuttle missions.

clue.text: Reportedly, European happy to provide dental appointment

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard, so a word for a European is said out loud

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic
up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: A cheerful European gives a talk about dentists.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine examination of the teeth by a dentist is a common example of a medical inspection.

clue.text: Travel adventurer

definitions.meaning: to travel on horseback or in a vehicle
Sally ... was the first American woman in space, in 1983

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for going along on a horse or bike, and the surname of a pioneering NASA astronaut.

clue.text: Belief in female setter, perhaps?

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, so it is an example
ma is a mother, a female parent

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, perhaps a woman, holds strong convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of principles laid down by an authority as unquestionably true is a fixed creed.

clue.text: Adventurer here, OK with vast ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An explorer arrives, says OK, and surveys the vast terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like land, but it is the past tense of grind. Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space, in 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme casts astronauts as adventurers; this Soviet cosmonaut flew Vostok 6 solo.

clue.text: Very much to say is set aside

indicators.note: to say means the words are heard, so a phrase meaning very much is spoken

parts.note: a lot means very much

explanation.surface: There is far too much to be said for saving.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot money or time is to earmark or assign it for a purpose, reserving it.

clue.text: Pumped-up Lebanese port?

parts.note: a Phoenician city on the coast of Lebanon shares its spelling with the inflated rubber ring of a wheel

explanation.surface: A puffed-up harbour town in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling of the wheel's rubber covering matches the ancient Lebanese city's name, so 'pumped-up' fits the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a port in southern Lebanon, while the same British word names the inflated wheel covering.

clue.text: A 20 needing no cab?

parts.note: 20 across is a ride; one carried on someone's back needs no taxi

explanation.surface: A trip that does not require a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 20 across gives 'a ride'; a lift on someone's shoulders needs no cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried on another person's back is a free lift, a ride taken without any vehicle.

clue.text: Not moving yet

definitions.meaning: nevertheless, as in 'even so, I stayed'

explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for being motionless and an adverb for nevertheless or even so.

clue.text: Two prepare for impact

definitions.meaning: a pair, especially of game birds, as in a pair of pheasants
to steady oneself against a coming shock

explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a pair, used of shot birds or pistols, and a verb for steadying oneself before a crash.

clue.text: Writer indeed struggling with books, financially needing others

indicators.note: the writing tool goes in the rearranged deed
struggling means thrashing about, so the letters of deed are shuffled

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A writer struggling with books has to rely on others for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be split into 'in' and 'deed': 'struggling' shuffles the second part to DEDE, and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who relies on others for financial support, such as a child, is reliant on them.
